question.text: Gopal, an institutional investor, uses a particular e-voting service provider's platform. After SEBI's single-login initiative through demat accounts, which category of shareholders may continue to use the existing login facility of e-voting service providers (ESPs)?

answer.text: Only retail individual shareholders holding shares in demat form
Physical shareholders and shareholders other than individuals (including institutional/corporate shareholders)
All shareholders regardless of category must use the single login
Only NRI shareholders and HUF holders

explanation.text: The Logic: After SEBI enabled single-login e-voting through demat accounts and the websites of Depositories/DPs, ESPs may continue the existing e-voting process for physical shareholders and shareholders other than individuals, including institutional/corporate shareholders. The Trap: It is tempting to assume the single-login mandate applies universally. The source-backed carve-out specifically preserves the existing ESP login for physical holders and non-individual shareholders. Note: The single-login facility is aimed at retail/public non-individual shareholders holding shares in demat form; the carve-out for physical and non-individual shareholders is the rule the workbook actually states.
